PullRequest.Title: Polish pinned session chat hierarchy connectors
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #332997

## Summary

- keep pinned/sticky session hierarchy guides aligned without shifting session content
- use continuous, rounded chat connectors with deliberate spacing before status icons
- use the higher-contrast tree guide token consistently to avoid visible shade changes
- normalize session chevron and phone-layout codicon sizing
- extend the existing component fixture to cover a pinned, sticky session with nested chats

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --grep "hierarchy guides"`
- `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/media/sessionsList.css`
- editor diagnostics and `git diff --check`

Scenarios.Scenario: Render, scroll, hover, and expand a pinned/sticky Sessions list row with nested chats on desktop or phone layout
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The WorkbenchObjectTree renders/reuses visible row templates, reactive code toggles existing sticky and hierarchy-guide classes, and Chromium performs style/layout/paint before the updated row is visible. The diff only changes fixed CSS declarations and pseudo-element geometry on this UI critical path; it adds no awaited or off-path work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with rendered sticky session rows and rendered expanded chat rows, not the full session history, because WorkbenchObjectTree row templates are virtualized/recycled. Each affected row still has a constant number of pseudo-elements; the last-chat change swaps which existing pseudo-element draws the branch rather than increasing cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DOM class updates and browser style/layout/paint run serially on the renderer main thread. No limiter, queue, IPC, subprocess, filesystem, database, or network operation is added or moved by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache or cache key changes. Warm row-template reuse remains intact, and cold versus warm rendering differs only through existing browser style/rendering caches; the changed declarations do not defeat template reuse or introduce negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the changed runtime lines are CSS declarations on existing selectors, surrounding renderer code proves classes are toggled on virtualized row templates, and no changed JavaScript executes in production.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact repaint duration and GPU raster cost vary by theme, device scale, and viewport, but the diff adds only constant border/background paint geometry and no selector expansion, animation, forced layout read, or extra DOM node, so there is no concrete regression mechanism despite those measurement uncertainties.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Replacing one sticky border with one pseudo-element and reshaping existing connector pseudo-elements preserves constant per-rendered-row work; tokenized font sizes and colors do not add hot-path computation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the themed Sessions component screenshot fixtures, including the pinned/sticky nested-chat hierarchy fixture
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Fixture setup synchronously creates in-memory mock sessions, builds pinned and sticky collections, instantiates the list, and renders the screenshot fixture. The added filter/map/flatMap traversals occur before fixture rendering and are on test execution's setup path only.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The added work is linear in each fixture's hard-coded session specification array. The changed hierarchy fixture has one session, and fixture inputs are bounded test data rather than user-controlled production collections.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fixture collection construction is synchronous and single-threaded; rendering then follows the existing component-fixture runner. No changed code adds parallel tasks, queues, IPC, subprocesses, filesystem access, database calls, or network requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is introduced or invalidated. Each fixture invocation constructs fresh mocks as before; pinned ID lookup is O(1) after one bounded setup traversal, and sticky wrappers are allocated only for marked fixture sessions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the file is under workbench test componentFixtures, the new values feed mocked services, and repository search found no production import of this fixture module.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The aggregate number of themed fixture invocations can vary by CI selection, but each invocation uses small static arrays and the code is excluded from shipped runtime paths.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The extra bounded in-memory fixture setup is test-only and negligible, while it enables the visual state under test.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all two changed files and all diff hunks. Traced runtime list rendering/virtualization, sticky and hierarchy-guide class updates, phone styling, and the component-fixture setup path. No diff-introduced hot-path, boundary-fanout, retention, cache-lifecycle, concurrency, or layout-thrashing regression met the reporting threshold.
